## Follow-up: parallel subagents hit a second, deeper fault on the same path

Since filing, I built a local normalizing proxy in front of the gateway and ran controlled experiments. New findings worth adding to this issue:

**Single subagent: fully working (via normalization).** With dotted/bare names rewritten into `(name, namespace)` pairs client-side, the complete spawn → wait → close loop succeeds repeatedly on `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` (6+ runs, CLI and Desktop). So the routing half is compensable.

**Parallel subagents: deterministically broken, not compensable.** When spawning a 2nd (or 3rd) subagent in the same session, the backend returns `spawn_agent` calls with **empty** arguments (`"arguments": ""`) — every time, 6/6 follow-up spawns observed. The 1st spawn of a session always carries a complete message; only repeats come back empty. There is no task message anywhere to recover, so no client-side transform can fix it.

**Control group pins it to this path.** The identical parallel prompt on `deepseek-v4.1-flash` behind the same gateway endpoint completes all 3 subagents end-to-end (greetings received, all closed, ~31k tokens). Same client, same tool list, same proxy — only the backend differs.

**Prompt-level mitigation does not help.** Adding an explicit instruction ("always emit complete valid JSON arguments, never emit empty ones") changed nothing: 6 consecutive empty spawns, then failure. Combined with the clean first-good/rest-empty split, this points away from prompt/task wording and toward either the model degrading on repeated same-name calls or the Meta adapter stripping arguments of repeated calls. The wire evidence cannot distinguish those two from outside — that part needs gateway-side logs.

Related argument-quality symptoms on the same path (all from the model/backend side, all absent on DeepSeek): `timeout_ms` emitted as float (`30000.0`, client expects i64 → local parse error) and inconsistent call-name spellings across turns (dotted once, bare the next). Empty history pairs subsequently fail upstream re-submission with `` `arguments` must be valid JSON `` (HTTP 400, `param: arguments`).

Net: single-subagent works around the routing bug; parallel multi-spawn needs a gateway-side fix. Happy to provide redacted request/response captures if useful.

Had the same issue

I'd like to work on this.

I traced the trigger on `dev` (the `1.18.31` line you're running) and the compaction you're seeing does not come from the token-based overflow check you'd expect:

- `packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts:495` is the check that agrees with your log: `needsCompaction` is set only when `isOverflow({ tokens: usage.tokens, ... })` is true. Since your log says `"overflow": false`, that is not the path firing.
- The path that *is* firing is the provider-error branch at `processor.ts:629`: a `ContextOverflowError` sets `ctx.needsCompaction = true` unconditionally, and the loop then returns `"compact"` (`processor.ts:693`) — an auto-compaction regardless of the client-side token math.
- That error is built in `packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts:685` from `ProviderError.parseAPICallError`, whose context-overflow test is a message match (`packages/opencode/src/provider/error.ts`, `isContextOverflow(m)` → `packages/llm/src/provider-error.ts`). Ollama's text lands on the `exceeds the available context size` pattern in that list, so your local model's server-side error is classified as a context overflow.

Two numbers disagree: the server's real window (Ollama `num_ctx` / the Modelfile) and `limit.context` in your `opencode.json` (32768). Every step the server rejects → opencode compacts → retries → rejected again, i.e. one compaction per tool call, each logged with `overflow: false`. That also explains why Copilot/Claude is unaffected: there the declared limit and the server window agree.

Plan:

1. reproduce with a custom `openai-compatible` provider whose declared `limit.context` is larger than the server's actual window, asserting that a provider-side overflow error produces at most one compaction instead of one per `step-finish` with `reason: "tool-calls"`;
2. break the loop: on the `ContextOverflowError` branch, do not start another auto-compaction when `isOverflow()` is false for the same model and token counts — record the provider error on the message and stop.

One question before I write it: should the client-side check win like that (stop compacting when it disagrees with the provider), or should the provider error be surfaced verbatim with both numbers (declared `limit.context` vs. the server's real window) so the misconfiguration is visible? My default is the first. Happy to have the issue assigned if that direction looks right.

Fix this code

**Docs validation + repro summary**

I validated my repro against the official docs, and they support that this is a mis-flag, not intended behavior:

1. `/docs/agents` — `plan` is a **built-in, first-party primary agent**, designed for analysis without modifications (edit/bash restricted). The JSON example even shows `plan` with `edit: deny, bash: deny` as a normal, valid config. A reduced toolset is documented and legitimate, not an abuse signal.
2. `/docs/agents — Permissions` — permissions gate **what the agent can execute**, not provider access. (This is @JaMoLpE88's point about how it *should* work — yet the repro below shows the gateway discriminating by toolset in practice.)
3. `/docs/zen` — Zen "works like any other provider"; free models are listed with **no per-agent restrictions**. No `User-Agent`, `x-opencode-session`, full-toolset, or SSE-only requirement is documented anywhere.
4. `/docs/agents — Tools (deprecated)` — per-agent `tools` is **deprecated** in favor of `permission`. If the gateway keys its access check off the request body `tools`, it would be gating on a field the docs themselves declare obsolete.

**Repro** (official CLI 1.18.31, Windows, free-tier `opencode/big-pickle`, same binary/session/model):

```sh
opencode run --agent build "Reply with exactly: PING-OK"  # → PING-OK ✅
opencode run --agent plan  "Reply with exactly: PING-OK"  # → "free tier can only be used from within OpenCode" ❌
```

Also fails with custom primary agents that only remove `bash` (`edit` allowed) — so it is the toolset shape, not one specific tool.

**Question for the team:** is rejecting first-party reduced-toolset agents on the free tier intended, or the same mis-flag class as the compaction bug (first-party, reduced toolset, mis-flagged) that was already fixed server-side? Either way, could the client requirements be documented, per @joaomj's request above?

Fixed by PR #48638. Backslash escapes are now canonicalized before path classification: the new `Wildcard.unquote` (`packages/core/src/util/wildcard.ts:21-60`, commit `77589d5d1a`) drops escapes exactly as the shell does, and `shell.ts:537-539` routes token classification through it (`expand()` at `shell.ts:598`). So `mkdir -p /tmp/my\ project/sub` resolves to the real in-project path and no longer emits an `external_directory` prompt; stored `always` patterns also use the unescaped spelling. Covered by `packages/core/test/wildcard.test.ts:122-127` and `packages/opencode/test/tool/shell.test.ts:484`. Follow-up on PR #48638 (`session-diff-events`, head `7063bdd9ea`).

Fixed by PR #48638. `packages/opencode/src/project/vcs.ts` now clamps requested diff context to `MAX_PATCH_CONTEXT_LINES = 1_000_000` (`:11-14`, applied at `:110`, `:135`, `:139`, commit `a38c279be3`), avoiding the `2 × INT32_MAX` hunk-merge overflow so git emits the file once instead of once per changed cluster. Regression test: *"diff('git') bounds the requested context so a file is emitted once"* in `packages/opencode/test/project/vcs.test.ts`. Follow-up on PR #48638 (head `7063bdd9ea`).

Fixed by PR #48638 (the branch already contains the rebased commits of the closed PR #48537). `SessionSummary.summarize` no longer re-attaches patch text to the user message: the durable baseline carries `diffs: []` (`packages/opencode/src/session/summary.ts:243`), patch payloads move to a dedicated `message.diff.updated` event (`summary.ts:249`), unchanged diffs are skipped (`summary.ts:212`), and superseded rows are tombstoned by the projector (`packages/core/src/session/projector.ts:247-295`). Commits `3086653aff`, `35310f77c4`, `9c0aa5931e`, `e2772c810e`. Tests: `packages/opencode/test/server/session-message-diff-events.test.ts`, `packages/core/test/session-projector.test.ts`. Follow-up on PR #48638 (head `7063bdd9ea`).

Fixed by PR #48638 — the branch contains the rebased commits of the closed PR #48849 (`a6c93e6190`, `a4b668fdbb`, `65edc2cf5a`, `06f9304478`). The whole snapshot transaction is wrapped in cross-process `EffectFlock` (`packages/opencode/src/snapshot/index.ts:286-289`); native `index.lock` contention is retried with bounded jitter and then surfaced as a deduplicated `snapshot_index_lock_stuck` diagnostic without deleting an unknown-owner lock (`:97-171`); abandoned opencode-owned tokens are reclaimed only when the owner PID is provably dead (`:342-363`); corruption/empty-tree recovery and SHA-validated tree IDs are added (`:194-198`, `:627-657`); and session revert now aborts on snapshot failure (`session/revert.ts:71-76`). Tests: `packages/opencode/test/snapshot/snapshot-lock.test.ts`. Follow-up on PR #48638 (head `7063bdd9ea`).

Relates to PR #48638. On the branch head (`7063bdd9ea`), redirect targets are now scanned regardless of command count (`packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts:1939-1949` plus `addPath`/`ask` at `:1671-1686`, `:1487-1506`), so a bare redirect to an **external** path (`> /etc/x`) does raise the `external_directory` prompt. However, a bare redirect whose target is **inside** the project still yields zero scan patterns, so the `shell`-tool permission (`shell.ts:1506`) is not evaluated and a `"*": deny` rule does not block the write — the in-project repro in this issue is not fully closed. Wave commits `9c5eb44d12` … `7063bdd9ea`. No claim of full resolution.

Partially addressed by PR #48638. Snapshot cleanup now runs `git gc --auto` under the local gate and treats any gc failure as non-fatal: a non-zero exit logs `cleanup failed` and returns, and the whole cleanup is sandboxed (`packages/opencode/src/snapshot/index.ts:582-602`). A competing/stale `gc.pid.lock` therefore no longer aborts the session. Git's native `gc.pid` coordination is relied upon deliberately (the cross-process snapshot flock intentionally does not wrap gc, `:290-291`), so there is no explicit retry/queue for `gc.pid.lock` itself. Follow-up on PR #48638 (head `7063bdd9ea`).

Confirming this bug on **v2.0.12** (also reproduced on v2.0.8) - Linux, logged into the OpenCode Console **and** ChatGPT OAuth (`chatgpt-headless`, Plus plan) at the same time.

Every `openai/*` model fails with `Provider request failed with HTTP 401`, and re-authenticating OpenAI does not help.

I verified the diagnosis in this PR independently:

- The request **does** route to the correct endpoint — I proxied OpenCode's traffic: 10 connections to `chatgpt.com:443`, zero to `api.openai.com`. The `chatgpt-account-id` header is present.
- But the `Authorization` bearer is the **Zen API key**, not the ChatGPT OAuth token. Curling `POST https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` with my Zen key reproduces the exact failure: `HTTP 401 {"message": "API keys are not supported by this endpoint.", "code": "api_key_not_supported"}`.
- My ChatGPT OAuth token itself is fine — the same request with the OAuth bearer returns `HTTP 200` and streams completions for `gpt-5.5` and `gpt-5.6-luna`. So the stored credential is valid; the provider just never sends it, exactly as described here.
- I also checked the `openai.ts` source at the `v2.0.11` and `v2.0.12` tags: the `integrationID` pin from this PR is absent in both, so no released version contains the fix yet.

Happy to test a build with this merged.

+1 for shipping this — it fixes a real production brick (Muse Spark sessions failing with `reasoning 'encrypted_content' was not issued to this caller` after idle-resume; the 400 was fatal and the session stayed stuck).

We vendored this recovery into our fork and verified it end-to-end. One detail worth noting: live sessions still drain through the V1 path (`packages/opencode` → `SessionProcessor` → `./llm`), not only the core runner — so we adopted both halves: your `packages/llm` classifier + core runner changes, and the `packages/opencode` side (`provider/error.ts` + `session/stale-reasoning.ts` + processor hook). Verified behaviors:

- rejection before output → exactly one retry; replayed request stripped of `reasoningEncryptedContent`/`itemId` on reasoning parts; visible text preserved
- second failure → surfaced, exactly 2 requests, no loop
- rejection after assistant output started → no recovery, no strip
- classifier matches the live `APICallError` text (`... was not issued to this caller`) and `invalid_encrypted_content`

Regression on our branch: opencode `test/session/` 452/0, provider dir 722/0, core 1138/0, llm 300/0; typechecks clean. Carried in `AceRothstein71/opencode` `session-diff-events` (`3d6de47fc6` core side, `b25cd68045` V1 port) — happy to drop or keep it rebased once this or #48908 lands. Thanks for the fix.

Adding quantitative data from a real-world macOS case (Desktop 1.18.31, Apple M3, external 2560x1600 @160Hz HiDPI). Confirms the loop is self-sustaining and independent of streaming activity:

- Renderer process accumulated **40h02m CPU time over 53h of uptime (~76% average)**; GPU helper 36h19m (~68%). The burn is continuous, not bursty.
- `renderer.log` over the same 2d5h window: **1416 `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` errors**. Per-minute breakdown by concurrent streaming sessions (correlated from the server log):
  - 0 streaming sessions: 141 minutes with errors, mean 9.8/min, peak 82/min
  - 1 session: 5 min, mean 2.4/min
  - 2+ sessions: 8 min, mean 3.4/min
  - Streaming was active in only ~9% of minutes in the window.
- So the error storm (and the CPU burn) runs **while nothing is streaming** - the loop is self-sustaining once entered, matching the "ongoing condition" description in #43355.
- After force-quit + relaunch: first error **26 seconds** after launch; 25 errors in the first 2 minutes; renderer/GPU back to ~37-60% CPU within 2 minutes. Restart does not clear the condition.

This suggests the dominant cost is the idle self-sustaining loop rather than streaming-driven re-rendering, so the rAF-defer / size-delta threshold guard proposed in #33712 would remove most of the sustained burn.

Confirming the "ongoing condition" and adding post-restart data (Desktop 1.18.31, macOS, Apple M3):

- The ResizeObserver storm runs continuously even with **zero active sessions**: in a 2d5h window, 141 of the error-bearing minutes had no streaming activity at all (mean 9.8 errors/min, peak 82/min), vs 2.4-3.4/min when sessions were streaming.
- After force-quit + relaunch the condition returns almost immediately: first error 26s after launch, 25 errors within 2 minutes, renderer/GPU processes back to ~37-60% CPU within 2 minutes. So the freeze-prone state is re-entered within seconds of startup, not only after turns finish.
- Renderer accumulated ~40h CPU over 53h uptime (~76% average), consistent with the loop running essentially the whole time.

This matches the timeline pattern reported here (error flood escalating into full freeze) and suggests the loop is entered at startup/first render and persists; turn completion is one escalation trigger among several.

Adding a data point from Desktop (Electron) 1.18.31 on macOS that supports the per-event re-render hypothesis and separates it from the idle ResizeObserver loop (#38296):

- With 2-3 concurrent streaming sessions, the Desktop renderer bursts to ~178% CPU (near 2 cores) and the GPU helper to ~40-60%; load tracks streaming activity and falls when sessions idle.
- Crucially, during streaming the ResizeObserver error rate *drops* (mean 2.4-3.4/min) vs when idle (mean 9.8/min, peak 82/min). So the streaming-time load is dominated by real re-render work (this issue), while the idle-time load is the self-sustaining ResizeObserver loop (#38296). The two regimes are separable in logs by error rate.
- Consistent with "per-event timeline re-rendering without batching": load scales with number of concurrent sessions and event rate.

Suggests the batching/throttling fix here and the ResizeObserver guard in #38296 address two distinct cost components; fixing only one leaves the other.
